example.name: organize_invoice_pdfs
example.description: Organize a collection of invoice PDFs by company and date
example.context: User has a folder with 50+ invoice PDFs from different companies, all with generic names like "Invoice_001.pdf"

step.action: Analyze sample files to understand content structure
step.code: read_file path="invoices/Invoice_001.pdf" # Extract text content read_file path="invoices/Invoice_002.pdf" # Compare patterns
step.explanation: Check for common patterns like company names, dates, invoice numbers

step.code:
#!/bin/bash # organize_invoices.sh for file in *.pdf; do # Extract company name and date using OCR/metadata company=$(pdfgrep -i "company|invoice from" "$file" | head -1 | sed 's/.*: *//') date=$(pdfgrep -i "date|invoice date" "$file" | head -1 | sed 's/.*: *//')
if [ -n "$company" ] && [ -n "$date" ]; then # Create directory structure mkdir -p "organized/${company}" # Rename file with descriptive name mv "$file" "organized/${company}/Invoice_${company}_${date}.pdf" fi done
step.explanation: Create a bash script to extract metadata and organize files
Run the organization script in the invoices directory
Check that files are properly organized and renamed

example.name: category_based_organization
example.description: Automatically categorize files by content analysis
example.context: User has mixed file types that need to be sorted into categories like Work, Personal, Finance, etc.

step.code: # Define categories and keywords declare -A categories=( ["Finance"]="invoice|receipt|bank|payment|salary|tax|budget" ["Work"]="meeting|project|report|presentation|email|memo" ["Personal"]="photo|vacation|recipe|personal|family|diary" ["Legal"]="contract|agreement|legal|lawsuit|court|attorney" )

#!/bin/bash # categorize_files.sh
# Define categories declare -A categories=( ["Finance"]="invoice|receipt|bank|payment|salary|tax|budget" ["Work"]="meeting|project|report|presentation|email|memo" ["Personal"]="photo|vacation|recipe|personal|family|diary" ["Legal"]="contract|agreement|legal|lawsuit|court|attorney" )
# Function to categorize file categorize_file() { local file="$1" local content=""
# Extract content based on file type if [[ "$file" == *.pdf ]]; then content=$(pdftotext "$file" - 2>/dev/null || echo "") elif [[ "$file" == *.txt ]] || [[ "$file" == *.md ]]; then content=$(cat "$file") fi
# Check against categories for category in "${!categories[@]}"; do if echo "$content" | grep -qi "${categories[$category]}"; then mkdir -p "$category" mv "$file" "$category/" echo "Moved $file to $category/" return 0 fi done
# If no category matches, put in Uncategorized mkdir -p "Uncategorized" mv "$file" "Uncategorized/" echo "Moved $file to Uncategorized/" }
# Process all files for file in *; do if [ -f "$file" ]; then categorize_file "$file" fi done
step.explanation: Create script to categorize files based on content keywords

step.code: execute_command command="cd mixed_files && bash categorize_files.sh" list_files path="mixed_files" recursive="true"

expected_output.structure: mixed_files/ ├── Finance/ │ ├── bank_statement.pdf │ └── tax_return.pdf ├── Work/ │ ├── project_plan.docx │ └── meeting_notes.txt ├── Personal/ │ ├── vacation_photos.jpg │ └── family_recipe.pdf └── Uncategorized/ └── random_file.txt

example.name: duplicate_file_cleanup
example.description: Find and handle duplicate files during organization
example.context: User has duplicate files that need to be identified and cleaned up

step.code: execute_command command="cd files && find . -type f -exec md5sum {} \; | sort | uniq -w32 -d"
step.explanation: Use md5sum to find files with identical content

step.code:
#!/bin/bash # deduplicate_files.sh
# Create backup directory mkdir -p backup_duplicates
# Find and process duplicates find . -type f -exec md5sum {} \; | sort | uniq -w32 -d | cut -d' ' -f3- | while read -r file; do # Keep the first occurrence, move others to backup if [ ! -f ".duplicate_processed$(basename "$file")" ]; then touch ".duplicate_processed$(basename "$file")" else echo "Moving duplicate: $file" mv "$file" "backup_duplicates/" fi done
# Clean up temporary files rm .duplicate_processed*
echo "Deduplication complete. Duplicates moved to backup_duplicates/"
step.explanation: Create script to identify and move duplicate files

step.code: execute_command command="cd files && bash deduplicate_files.sh" list_files path="files/backup_duplicates"
step.explanation: Run deduplication and check backup folder

expected_output.summary: Removed 15 duplicate files, kept originals, duplicates backed up
